SMTO-EXE-0013 — SMTO didn't repeat commands that already ran

GUID: e7ee139b-ea10-4cb8-8e95-848c6f297285
Slug: partial-sequence-replay-blocked
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • Some commands in a series already ran earlier in this task. SMTO refused to run the whole series again from the start so those finished commands aren't done twice.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task in the conversation and see which commands in the series finished, which failed, and which never started. Finished commands' changes are already in place, so running them again could duplicate or undo work.
  2. If any command shows an unknown result, check its change yourself on that computer, for example whether the file or program it was adding is there. SMTO can't tell whether an interrupted command made its change, so you need to confirm it.
  3. Tell SMTO in the conversation which commands are already done and ask it to continue with only the rest. SMTO will then run just the unfinished commands instead of the whole series.

What success looks like

  • The task carries on with the remaining commands and finishes without rerunning the earlier ones.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to rerun the whole series from the beginning until you've confirmed that repeating the finished commands is safe.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A shell sequence was re-proposed after a partially completed or interrupted attempt in the same state version; the runtime blocked replaying the whole sequence because some of its child commands already executed.

What this means

  • The runtime found a previously completed sequence prefix or an interrupted sequence with retained child receipts and refused to replay those children as a fresh whole sequence. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The runtime found a previously completed sequence prefix or an interrupted sequence with retained child receipts and refused to replay those children as a fresh whole sequence.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect each retained child receipt and the verified prefix boundary; separate completed, uncertain and unstarted children.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the sequence's child receipts (completed, failed, outcome_unknown) for the run, resolve any unknown effects against the target, then issue only the remaining children (mutation.effectful_replay guard). Do not replay completed mutating steps; a full rerun is only allowed with an explicit unsafe grant.
  • Inspect preserved receipts and resume from the verified boundary and current state. Do not replay completed mutating steps.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Recovery preserves completed children and schedules only justified remaining work under current authority.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
